POWL is a priority underfollowed candidate for the electrical sub-node: medium-voltage switchgear, behind-the-meter data-center electrical gear, and backlog/order inflection need deeper verification.

NVT is a priority underfollowed candidate for rack/white-space infrastructure: enclosures, bus systems, intelligent PDUs, and liquid-cooling platforms make it a plausible second-order AI infrastructure beneficiary.

MOD is a priority underfollowed candidate for data-center cooling: fiscal filings and transcript evidence support data-center cooling growth, but later layers must separate durable AI exposure from general HVAC/thermal cyclicality.

The power/thermal balance-of-plant node has evidence of real chokepoint behavior: switchgear, transformers, batteries, cooling systems and installation complexity can delay data-center capacity even when compute hardware is available.

Layer 2 should verify market-cap buckets, current analyst coverage, data-center revenue mix, customer concentration, and whether backlog is AI-specific versus broader electrification, LNG, utility or industrial demand.

MOD should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a thermal balance-of-plant candidate because its SEC filing explicitly links data-center cooling demand to AI/HPC-driven heat loads and hybrid/liquid cooling.

BELFB is a speculative-shadow candidate: market cap and obscurity fit the underfollowed lens, but later layers must verify material AI/data-center revenue, design wins, and whether power-conversion components are supply constrained.

For this node, the strongest early evidence appears in companies disclosing backlog, megaproject bookings, data-center cooling capacity, or explicit AI/HPC heat-load commentary rather than generic electrification language.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found one high-attention reference leader and three plausible underfollowed direct-exposure candidates tied to AI data-center power and cooling balance-of-plant. The strongest direct evidence is Vertiv for integrated power/liquid-cooling systems, Powell Industries for medium-voltage switchgear and data-center megaproject backlog, nVent for liquid cooling, power distribution and bus systems, and Modine for data-center cooling growth including liquid-cooling-related offerings. This is not a buy/sell list; it is a research universe for later Serenity evidence, pricing, and falsification layers. Layer 1B expansion for the AI data-center electrical/thermal balance-of-plant node. The reference lane is represented by Vertiv as the obvious pure-play anchor in critical power, cooling, monitoring, and services. The underfollowed lane emphasizes less-obvious US-listed suppliers where AI data-center demand may appear through medium-voltage switchgear, engineered power distribution, thermal systems, liquid-cooling capacity, and smaller power-conversion components rather than through headline semiconductor exposure. This is a research universe expansion only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the universe for the data-center electrical and thermal balance-of-plant node using a two-lane funnel. Vertiv is retained as the high-attention reference anchor because its public disclosures directly map to busway, UPS, CDU, liquid cooling and monitoring. The underfollowed lane emphasizes smaller or less AI-labeled suppliers with evidence of data-center demand: Powell Indus
